prompt: A quantity grows by $10\%$ each year. What growth factor do you multiply by each year? (Write it as a decimal.)
hint: After the growth you still have all of the original amount, plus a bit extra. What percent of the original is that in total?

hints.text: After the growth you still have all of the original amount, plus a bit extra. What percent of the original is that in total?
Keeping $100\%$ and gaining $10\%$ gives $100\% + 10\% = 110\%$. Change that percent to a decimal by dividing by $100$.
$110\%$ written as a decimal is $1.10$, so the growth factor is $1.10$.

explanation: Growing by $10\%$ means the new amount is the whole old amount plus a tenth more, which is $110\%$ of it.
To write a percent as a decimal, divide by $100$: $110\% = 1.10$.
So each year the quantity is multiplied by the growth factor $1.10$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test it on $100
steps: What times 100 gives 110? 110 ÷ 100 = 1.10 — that is the factor.

alternativeExplanations.title: Keep-plus-gain picture
steps: Picture the amount as a full bar (the 1) plus a small extra slice (the 0.10).
